ety.text: First attested in 1705. Borrowed from Polish apartament, from French appartement, from Italian appartamento.

x: Зво́нкие пру́тья тяжёлой строи́тельной армату́ры, свиса́я с платфо́рм как хвосты́, греме́ли так, бу́дто толка́ли вперёд маши́ны.

ety.text: Ultimately from Latin armatura. First attested in 1703.
Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic гласити (glasiti), from Proto-Slavic *golsiti. By surface analysis, глас (glas) + -и́ть (-ítʹ). Doublet of голоси́ть (golosítʹ).

x: Он вхо́дит в го́рло, он ре́жущий зонд, Забы́вший о сострада́ньи. Он спазм уку́са в диафра́гмовый зонт, Испо́лненный ожида́нья

s.g: suitably, adequately, in an appropriate/adequate/proper manner

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic зълчь (zŭlčĭ) (rarer жълчь (žŭlčĭ)), from Proto-Slavic *zьlčь (“bile”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źulʔ-, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰlh₃-. Related to *zelenъ and was under the influence of *žьltъ.

s.g: to stall, to falter, to come to a halt, to face a standstill (to stop moving, working, progressing or increasing)
to obscure, to dim, to cloud, to fog

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zvěrinъ. By surface analysis, зверь (zverʹ) + -и́ный (-ínyj).

s.g: to spoil, to ruin, to deform, to mar

x: И расчёт его́ стратеги́ческий по́лностью подтверди́лся, терпе́ние его́ и скро́мность в выраже́ниях бы́ли вознаграждены́: три судака́ ве́сом по кило́ лежа́ли на льду и ско́рбно глазе́ли в не́бо оловя́нными зрачка́ми.

В отли́чие от болтуно́в ме́лкой буржуази́и, эсе́ров и меньшевико́в, пролетариа́т бу́дет твёрдо знать, в чём состои́т на де́ле «проры́в на фро́нте» кла́ссовой борьбы́, обезвреже́ние врага́, обезвреже́ние эксплуата́торов. Князь Львов помо́г пролетариа́ту позна́ть э́ту и́стину. Поблагодари́м кня́зя Ль…

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъnędzь, borrowed from Germanic, from Proto-Germanic *kuningaz. The feminine form княги́ня (knjagínja, “princess”) has preserved the original, Germanic g sound. Doublet of ксёндз (ksjondz), a borrowing from Polish, and ко́нунг (kónung).

s.g: triangular headscarf (traditionally of calico), kerchief, babushka
coffee (in the form of a beverage)

ety.text: First attested in late 17th or early 18th century. Borrowed from a West Germanic language, either English coffee, German Koffee, or directly from Dutch koffie, Ultimately from Italian caffè, from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa). Doublet of кафе́ (kafé).

s.g: masculine (having male qualities, not feminine or effeminate)
to disclose, to show, to reveal, to display
to discover, to find out, to detect, to reveal, to spot

ety.text: Possibly related to Ancient Greek φελλός (phellós, “cork”).

s.g: sharpness (quality of being sharp (as a knife))
ellipsis of пе́рвое блю́до (pérvoje bljúdo): starter (first course of a meal)
to overdo, to spoil by overdoing
to digest (separate food in its passage through the alimentary canal)
to digest, to process (think over and arrange methodically in the mind)

ety.text: From пере- (pere-) + вари́ть impf (varítʹ). Compare Ukrainian перевари́ти (perevarýty).

s.g: intentional distortion of ideas, facts, data, etc. to hide contradictions, theft, etc.

ety.text: From подгон- (podgon-) + -ка (-ka). Derived from the present tense stem подгон- (podgon-) of подогна́ть (podognátʹ).

s.g: to connect (to), to make a connection (to)
to get involved (in), to join in
section of multiapartment building with common entrance

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic подъѣздъ (podŷjězdŭ). Action noun from подъе́хать (podʺjéxatʹ, “to approach”), from под- (pod-) + е́хать (jéxatʹ). Compare Ukrainian під'їзд (pidʺjizd).

s.g: to keep silent, to be silent (for a while)
direction, way, manner, path, vein, course (of development of a situation)

ety.text: Presumably related to Lithuanian rusė́ti (“to flow”), rusnóti (“to flow slowly”). Compare the name of the Lithuanian river Raũsvė, and Rusni̇̀s, a right distributary of the Neman.

s.g: Sardinia (an island and autonomous region of Italy, in the Mediterranean Sea)
squeezer (for making juice out of fruits or vegetables), juicer
Orthetrum cancellatum, the black-tailed skimmer, a species of dragonfly.

x: Ему́ да́ли жи́рного мясно́го су́пу и ло́моть хле́ба.

ety.text: Borrowed from French soupe. Further from Latin suppa.

s.g: to transmit, to broadcast, to relay

ety.text: Evidently backformed from трансля́ция (transljácija) (ultimately from Latin trānslatiō), with the suffix -и́ровать (-írovatʹ).

s.g: to safeguard (against), to guard (against), to keep (from), to preserve (from)
Fusha, Modern Standard Arabic, Classical Arabic
